prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Distributed Systems Glossary (language en).
Grid: 3 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Term" · longest unbreakable word 99px · one-line width 152px
  col 2: header "Definition" · longest unbreakable word 108px · one-line width 1472px
  col 3: header "Example" · longest unbreakable word 83px · one-line width 814px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Define distributed-systems terms and illustrate each with an example.","reading":"Readers scan the first column for a term, then read across its row to connect the definition with the example. Wrapped lines should remain easy to associate with their row.","groups":["Definition and Example are companion prose columns: one explains the term and the other makes it concrete.","Term is the row identifier and needs enough prominence to support scanning."],"keep_intact":["Individual words and technical identifiers, especially long terms and unbreakable words in the prose.","The association between each term, its definition and its example."],"may_wrap":["Multiword terms can wrap between words.","Definitions and examples can wrap naturally at word boundaries; longer cells can absorb additional lines in the other cells of the same row."]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r2A: widths [120, 136, 103] · table 360×2360px · row heights [36, 315, 315, 339, 315, 315, 315, 408] · column headers wrapped 0/3 · tallest cell 17 lines · mid-word splits 1
Design r2B: widths [120, 134, 105] · table 360×2384px · row heights [36, 315, 315, 339, 339, 315, 315, 408] · column headers wrapped 0/3 · tallest cell 17 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2C: widths [119, 137, 103] · table 360×2314px · row heights [36, 292, 315, 339, 315, 315, 315, 385] · column headers wrapped 0/3 · tallest cell 16 lines · mid-word splits 1

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
